Bug-addled and set up to fail.
I'll start with the positives:
-Beautiful design
-ingenious concept of 'stay still for defence'
-light as your only defence
-keep moving to 'charge' your weapon
-everyone is in it to win or die
-immersive pov
Negatives:
-set lifespan of the entire game
-the 'hunter' camera moves like you're either drunk, concussed or about to throw up from motion sickness
-buggy as hell
-VERY overpriced for a 'all on one' deathmatch game
I'm just going to quote a few lines from the dev blog:
"There's no denying or hiding this, we simply made some mistakes with The Flock."
(about the 'life count') "and will stick with, even if and until it means the end of the game or company"
I thought the 'set number of lives' was a joke... Not a very funny one either.
Name one game where global permadeath is a positive feature?
When they made mario, they didn't say 'when you die X times, the game won't work anymore' because, well, NOBODY WOULD BUY IT!
I got this game as a gift and consider it a pretty poor gift.
I would pick this game up for a few quid if it were versus AI or someting. or the life-count' was yearly... but I would not pay the full price under any circumstances. I would not recomend this game even without the deathcount. With the deathcount? It's practically an insult of our inteligence to assume we'd pay this much for something that is openly going to run out!
The controls are simple enough, but the 'hunter' moves around so much that I get a headache
I get that a moving camera is meant to make us feel more agitated and immersed in the game... but motion-sick isn't immersion.
I like the light-artifact. It's a cool idea and a very interesting weapon... but when it just conks out at random and doesn't seem to have an explanation why? That sounds to me like a liability in a game where everyone else is out to get you!
'yay! doing real well! hanging in ther... oh... nope. need to change the bulb... well, crap'
All you need to do is hang around for that to happen and voila!
the 'all or nothing' works in small doses. but for the one problem that the only person who is under attack is 'it' and you become 'it' by killing them. why bother until they're near the end and the others chasing him have gone down in flames?
Surely, its just going to be a waiting match for the next-to-last-one-standing and then jump 'em? (see broken light artifact for how)
The biggest problem is lifespan. I can't see this game being enjoyable for more than a few playthoughs... that kind of short-term 'oh, that was fun... now let's play a proper game' feeling is really dissapointing when you look at the detail that has gone into this!
I want to like it! I really do! I want to enjoy the hunt, the chase, to fight for my life and battle to take theirs... but instead, it's just 'ok. that's the entire gameplay in one match. now i've completed this, what now?'
Not to mention that in the entire time playing I didn't get a single other person in a match! I could not find anyone.
Pretty sure that the lifespan of this game is going to last far longer than I anticipate because for it to diminish, someone needs to play it!

Shadow Warrior is a game you should buy. Its story is surprisingly excellent and the gameplay is excellent as well.
Story:
I say the story is surprisingly excellent because the original Shadow Warrior had an awful story and the dialogue was mostly dumb middle school sex jokes. This game's story is unique (at least to me) and at the end you might shed a tear or two. While Hoji at first seems like the comic relief character it is later revealed that he is more involved in the events of the game than you think.
Gameplay:
I played this game on Hard so the effectiveness of the weapons is based on hard mode.
This is a hack and slash / FPS game. Your sword is incredibly useful and you can perform Ki moves with it like a thrust, a spin attack and a sword beam attack. You can also use Ki to create a shield, a net to float enemies, and an energy attack. While the sword moves are useful the latter is not. I fully upgraded the net and it doesn't last long enough for you to do any significant damage that you could've done without charging it up. The shield is OK but you can already regenerate your health and it doesn't allow you to use Ki moves with your sword or certain special modes of your guns (anything that requires the RMB). The shield at least might be more useful in insane mode. You can purchase new modes for your gun like sticky bombs for your crossbow, a firing mode for your revolver and more. I would like to say that your shotgun is super weak. It does barley any damage against bigger enemies in Hard and it has a long reload time. A shielded enemy needed 3 firestorm attacks (both barrels) to die so even with the quad pack I would still have to reload. Here is a tip: In the luck section buy the richman I and richman II at the start of the game. Later on it gets more difficult to obtain Karma Points and without Richman the game will be less fun since you will never make enough to get the gun upgrades you want.
The gameplay works like Fear. You walk forward, fight enemies and if you stray from the path you might find a secret with money or karma. You have regenerating health but you have to activate it by double tapping the D key and holding RMB. Doing this in the middle of combat is very intense. In combat while you do your Ki moves you can still use your guns and sword and even reload the former. So the combat involves alot of multitasking and hectic shooting and slashing.
While some of the weapons and moves are useless to me they might be useful to others. Either way I had a fun time with this game and was surprised that the story was really good. In the game credits they place the credits of the original game despite only sharing its premise. This is a completely original game and you should definitely check it out.

TL/DR - If you like Cyberpunk, dystopian-like futures, well paced stories and character development, then you could do a lot worse than Technobabylon. (Love the reference to Big Blue Cup)
I find a lot of point and click adventures to be a little tiresome these days, some are a little too rooted in conventions set by their predecessors, while others find themselves wrapped up in overly convoluted and obtuse puzzles. Technobabylon manages to find some fresh perspective on these puzzles, keeping most of their components within reasonable grasp and still manage to deliver a fantastic plot with engaging characters at the end of it all.
Presentation is beautifully executed, as i have come to expect with Wadjet Eye games, thus enables the player give in and throw themselves into the experience completely. Amazing. one of the few games in recent years to pull me in.
If you enjoy games with tons of content, that are actually challenging, and are completely polished, look no further.
Hollow knight manages to tell one of the most compelling stories that I've witnessed in a game, with no narration or hour long cut scenes. It's probably the minimalism that makes it so unique, the moments that stick with you are stuble and are a fleeting moment. Looking out a window into a dead city, watching a friend turn into one of the monsters you've become so numb to slaughtering in the hundreds, corpses hudled together in a corner of the map.
For me these felt more real than any story based game I've experienced.
Which is funny because this isnt really a story based game, it has some of the smoothest combat I've seen. Just when you've started to grasp how to fight enemies with minimal damage in an area, you're thrown a curveball: a new area with completely different enemies, coming back to an area only to find all the bugs have changed their appearance and fighting style.  When you do something badass, you feel badass. Probably because the controls are so tight every movement feels like your own. Every counter feels like your design, because it is! There isnt a set way to beat any boss or counter a certain move, you make your own way: meticulously sidestep your opponent until an oppourtunity arises, or go in full rambo swinging your nail left and right hitting anything that moves.
Yet it probably isn't the combat or the story that makes this game top notch in my opinion, its the feeling of discovery. Every corner could bring a new fight, or a secret passage. Every new area only connects to other new ones waiting to be explored. Every small victory is rewarded, every act of curiostity is well spent. I have spent hours just aimlessly exploring the huge game world, finding as many nooks and small peices of lore as I could. Only to think "I wonder if there is something over there" when looking at my map, and finding a whole new game area. This is why this game is so special to me, why I hope to 100% it, and continue to when the amazing devs release more content.
(if anyone is wondering why I have so little hours, I spent 35 hours on a pirated copy before finally saying to myself that this game is a masterpiece and I needed to own it for real)

This game contains different fun elements:
- beautiful character design & environment + fitting music
- natural voice acting (although the way it was scripted made some reactions seem over-the-top)
- well written dialogue (made sense)
- multiple & meaningful character introductions
- intuitive & original puzzles (with some exceptions, but definitely doable)
- flashbacks
- choice & consequence
- virtual reality & AI theme
- ethnical diversity
- taboo & shocking details
There's a total of 3 main characters (which are each playable at some point, and even interchangeably so near the end, so as to have them act as a team - very fun!).
Just wished they had implemented that possibility sooner!
I pretty much loved everything about this game :). I could see myself replaying it over & over again in a couple of years from now!
This game gave me the chills (in a good way), the way Blade Runner did back in the day! It's so refreshing & different!

(This is a joint review of CSX Heavy Haul, Great Western Express and Rapid Transit, but bear in mind I never really play Heavy Haul.)
Pros:
- Looks fantastic graphics-wise.
- Being able to walk around in a train simulator is awesome.
- Locomotives are highly detailed and seem very accurate.
- Everything surrounding the track actually looks realistic and has detail, unlike previous simulators.
- Tutorials are fully narrated and informative.
Cons:
- Could be optimised better (FPS is bearable, but by no means satisfactory, and that's with a high-end PC).
- Mediocre sound design.
- Content is lacking for the price (if you do buy, I'd highly recommend getting it on sale).
- Quite a few major bugs.
- DLC is being added before the base game is in a finished state (note that by DLC I mean individual locomotives and such, not the full expansions like GWE and Rapid Transit).
- Lack of basic options (mouse sensitivity, field of view).
Don't get me wrong, the game is well-made in terms of realism, but in my eyes recommending it would imply the developers don't have a lot to fix and improve, which is most definitely not the case. When I can confidently say 'this is worth the price' I'll switch my review.

Shadowgrounds was a pretty doesn't shooter a few years ago, but Survivor doesn't really do much new, and is pretty boring. As a top down shooter you play as a marine who is trying to escape a ruined base that is overrun by aliens. The weapons are pretty generic with shotguns, assault rifles, flamethrowers, grenades etc. You can pick up health packs, ammo, and OK you know this formula already.
Unlike other better shooters like Alien Shooter the game doesn't even offer intense moments. There are a few straggling aliens coming after you and maybe a few hard ones, and that's it. You can easily kill these guys and it doesn't feel very satisfying at all. You can shoot barrels, toss grenades, or just run around holding the fire button and you'll beat these guys. Ammo is plentiful so you never feel like you're "surviving" and it's pretty hard to die.
There is an upgrade system that you use by finding "parts" and when you level up you can use points for different upgrades like sonar, health boosts etc., and each character you play has the same upgrades? That's pretty lame. While each character has a different load out there's just nothing exciting about it at all. The game is fun however since it's good for more casual players who don't like the intensity of other top down shooters, but even the aliens are generic looking. Instead of creepy deformed things you just get typical bug like aliens.
The game doesn't look or sound too good either, and the music almost seems non existent while the game looks pretty bland. The level design is also pretty bad since I wandered around areas and didn't know where to go like shooting a glass panel to open a walkway. There is no hint, the panel doesn't even light up or flash. So this is bad level design, and the whole freaking game just feels boring! The game is a little fun if you're bored or just want a decent top down shooter.

The one criticism I have which has not changed is the sound. I’m not a professional racer, I don’t know what it sounds like to be behind the wheel of one of these monstrosities, but when I play a racing game with a 5.1 surround system I expect it to feel raw and powerful. Instead, I found all of the vehicles to sound unbelievably anemic and whiny. Again, I have no idea what these cars may sound like in real life, but this is a game. It’s disappointing to see such aggressive speed machines yet hear whiny little RC cars.
Now one of the first things I learn was that this is (at least in some capacity) the same people responsible for Race07. I recently gave that game a whirl and had a nauseatingly terrible experience with it. Whatever they learned from those past titles they have clearly refined it and mastered it for RaceRoom. I know a lot of time has passed between the two, but it’s hard to think this quality sim is from the same people behind Race07. Great job, devs; keep up the iteration and self improvement!
The next thing I took a step back from complaining about was the Free-to-Play model. Many of the negative reviews pointed out the frankly incomprehensible way in which content is being sold. I think the model is confusing and poorly thought out, but I don’t think the fact that you are expected to pay for the majority of the cars when the game and a handful of vehicles are completely free is a point to merit a negative review. The game is extremely detailed and - as best I can tell - extremely faithful to the physics behind circuit racing. RaceRoom isn’t a Free-to-Play racing game in my eyes; it’s a demo for a well crafted racing simulator that allows you to pay for exactly the content you want if you decide that the mechanics interest you.
I didn’t much enjoy it, but RaceRoom Racing Experience is a free demo for a very high quality racing simulator. If you’re into this genre and like what you see in the screenshots, you should absolutely try out the game. There is literally nothing to lose by trying it out.

Who is this Game For?
==================
It’s hard to point to any one single aspect of Call of Duty as the reason that it is such an enjoyable game. It’s not a particularly innovative game, but rather does an excellent job of bringing together all of the best facets of World War II shooters and wrapping it all in top-notch level design. Who cares about innovation when you’re having so much fun? Anyone who’s a fan of FPS or the Call of Duty series in general should give the game a try, picking it up when discounted on Steam.
Is it good?
=================
Call of Duty provides a mix of realism and arcade elements that work together nicely to provide a great gameplay experience.  A well-placed shot or two will be able to bring you down, but you can actually take a fair amount of damage and there are health packs scattered about the level or dropped by the dead that can restore you to full strength. If the game's missions could be described in a word, that word would be intense.  Right from the start you'll be in the thick of things, outnumbered and facing withering fire from the enemy.  In just the first few missions you'll have to assault bunkers, take out Wirbelwind Flakpanzers protected by machine gun nests, and face the devastating fire of a Tiger tank's cannon and machine gun.  If you think that's tough, wait until you reach the Russian missions.  In a sequence obviously inspired by Enemy at the Gates, you'll have to cross the Volga River into the heart of the maelstrom in Stalingrad ... and do so without a gun.  Throughout the campaign the game doesn't let up, moving you from one action-packed mission to the next.
The game is also mod friendly with a pretty decent following still. There are a few interesting mods that improve just the graphics and sounds including Extreme Mod Light [2013] and CoD Realism Enhancement.
Does it have any problems?
========================
The game requires PunkBuster update to play on protected servers which are no longer hosted on EvenBalance's website. Even still, the multiplayer is actually pretty active for such an old game. Just make sure you get the United Offensive expansion pack since that’s where most of the multiplayer servers need.
A big word of warning though, a lot of people have experienced problems running the game on newer hardware, one of the biggest problems when trying to play older games. The biggest problem is a buffer overflow with newer Nvidia hardware and Intel HD cards
. These issues can be fixed, so if you do have errors, please check the PC Gaming Wiki link for the fix.
Final Thoughts!
====================
It was all too easy to peel away the layers of glitz and gloss and come up with a long list of inconsistencies, flaws and slightly irksome design decisions. Though, combining an authentic look, sound and feel with a simple interface and innovative game play mechanics it’s no wonder that this game spawned a legacy that has lasted till now and this game is still one of the best WWII FPS.

The Bridge is a puzzle game in a world inspired by M. C. Escher art. In each level you must exit a door. To reach the door you have to rorate the world which will change the gravitational direction and possibly turn the ceiling into the floor, just like in M. C. Escher art. It's an interesting puzzle with unusual mechanics. If you like puzzles this is a decent game.
+ Original concept
+ Carefully designed levels
+ Distinct levels
+ Polished art style
At first this game looked like an experimental artistic game, which would be fine too, but as soon as I started a level it was clear it was a puzzle game. The concept itself is very interesting in my opinion. In the first levels you are able to rotate the world and with that change the gravitational direction. Sometimes you must get keys to open doors, avoid obstacles or press buttons to exit the room, so you must be very careful when rotating the world because these items are also affected by gravitity. This can become complicated due to undesirable chain effects when rotating the world. Fortunately you can rewind you actions at any point without consequences.
The game will get more difficuly and complex as you go on. On later stages there are parallel worlds with different a gravitational directions than the regular world. In most levels you are able to see and collide with parallel world objects. To solve these puzzles you may have to change the gravitational direction of both worlds. It's not an easy game. You have to calculate every rotation and side effects in order to exit each room. After you beat the game you get the mirrored levels. These aren't simply mirrored but also have more obstacles than the regular levels. Don't skip these if you want a challenge.
There aren't any relevant flaws in the game. There are some pointless achievemets but other than that everything looks fine. The art style is nice, the character is easy to control and the music is always the same but it's not annoying. If you're into puzzles check this game out.

Amazing game with amazing story. It was emotionally evocative and had many dark moments and deaths, unlike any other Final Fantasy game. Keep in mind this used to be a PSP-game, so cutscenes aren't as good as you'd expect from a modern game, but they are still beyond acceptable, in my opinion. There's so many factors in this game, that I rather not mention due to prefer people playing and exploring them themselves. but this game is actually really huge, and even has a real-time training program.  14 playable characters + Eidolons (summonings). I love to go to practice arena and just play with different characters. Not to mention they all can go to level 99, and unlocking new ABILITIES along the way (under Promotion at the red crystals). As far as armament and promotion, the game was very poor to introducing those, and I found out about them after a while, but now I've gotten them, my experience rose up tenfold. Sooo many upgrades, fun unique abilities that can be upgraded in different aspects. Though, even at mediocre level, you shouldn't underestimate enemies; They can be freakingshly strong. Also keep in mind this game expects you to replay the game more than once or twice with the same save. There are some boss fights where even if you wipe with all characters, you'd still accomplish the mission. When you finish the game, you can take all your character progress into the replay and do it all again at mediocre level, and then once again at hard mode (+30 levels to all enemies). So this game pretty much takes a long time to completely finish.
As far as gameplay (I used keyboard/mouse), the camera took me a bit of time to get used to, but not more than 2 hours to perfect it. It seemed a bit messy at start, but once you get a hold on movement and targeting it's very easy, despite many others reviews saying otherwise. I have no problem targeting my desired target.  I can't say why some people has a problem with this, but thats just my experience.
Also, I recommend refusing back up from Akademia at first few missions and only play with your characters. At later missions, I'd recommend accepting back up, as the ally NPCs are high on level and can tank for you, and it wont cost you a casualty if they die (dying with all 14 characters results in game over).
back up from Akademia will result in your characters being randomly switched with ally NPCs in which you cannot control the NPC nor the switch. Though, you'll have a chance at seeing Kurasame (badass Commading Officer), and his pet Tonberry. Though, they'll only come in very dire situations.
Tl;Dr: Great game, amazing story. Take
time to explore game mechanics, the abilities/spells and world map, and practice with
characters. There will be numerous times where you'll get insta-shot at the beginning of a boss fight, and then you'd have to rely on your reserves. Also,
, at every red crystal, you should save. I'd recommend one save before a mission, and a second save at every red crystal during the mission, respectively. You can replay missions, but should you be unhappy with your previous checkpoint, this allows you to restart. Last, but not least; Watch the cutscenes and cinematics; the game is great at telling the amazing story.

Technobabylon is one of those games I bought on a whim and ended up absolutely LOVING. A believable setting, very well-written characters with great dialogue, challenging puzzles that avoid being illogical/downright infuriating and a story with just the right amount of twists and turns made this one of my favorite adventure games of recent memory.
The story is masterfully balanced between serious, heavy moments and enjoyable touches of levity/humor; it avoids being a grimdark nightmare like so many cyberpunk games, yet also doesn't rely on tongue-in-cheek references to genre classics to score nostalgia points. Technobabylon is simply a fantastic cyberpunk adventure game that stands on its own with the best the genre has to offer. If cyberpunk fiction is up your alley and you enjoy classic adventure games, I can't recommend this enough.
(I'd also love to see a sequel that explores Max and Dr. Regis' origin stories!)

A reasonably good game, held back by a lot of small flaws.

Combat itself is pretty easy, ~11 hours in and the most I've died to a boss is twice. It makes the game a lot less rewarding.
The combat also has little variety so far because the basic attack hasn't changed at all. Enemies do vary, but something about the game makes them still all feel more generic than other metriodvania games I've played.
With how round everything is, the hitboxes can be a bit odd, especially on units with long, thin parts on their body.
The map doesn't pause the game, and there's a slight delay to opening it.
Money flies around everywhere, and much of it ends up falling into pits/spikes/etc. Minor complaint but the things add up.
The game looks and sounds really good, but personally, idc aesthetic. The best part about this game is probably the movement. Ignoring some times where hitboxes are hard to see, the movement in this game is one of the most fluid of any game I've ever played. The first time I used the walljump, I was very pleasantly surprised. Any game without a good movement system suffers heavily because of it, and likewise this game is made a lot better because of it.
In the end, I would recommend it, because even though I feel the game could be much much better, it still has enough to offer and is gripping enough for me to play until completion. Purchases and a few modification things, along with the typical unlocking of new abilities, give a good sense of progression and the platforming has all been enjoyable.

I bought this game while it was on sale during the Summer Sale, it looked like a fun metroidvania, I loved the art style and my friend recommended it. So figured to get it. After some time I got to it and man, I was hooked. What hooked me was an unexpected level of detail into the games world, the highly interconnected map, all the little details built into each area that tells its own story, and rich lore that makes you feel for these poor little bugs and their dying world.
Like, it's kinda of a dying world sort of deal like Dark Souls, but with bugs! Cute little bugs. As such, the game is also quite difficult and is up there for difficult games. I'd set the games difficulty somewhere between castlevania and metroid games, though depending entirely if you're better at one over the other (I found it quite hard because im better at Metroid than Castlevania, and this game is very castlevania for the bosses). You have lots of ways to play though, there is something to suit every players style of play and even navigating the world will change depending on the player. Which adds to how real the world feels despite it being a cartoony if dark fantasy setting.
The gameplay as a whole is very tight metroidvania type fare, the animations are so fluid it's pretty easy to get a hang of enemies moves and stuff. Usually don't have to worry about a hit box being bigger than the enemy itself. Bosses are punishing, panic healing will get you no where in this game. There are "charms" that change how The Knight plays, and makes certain aspects of the game easier, or in my opinion, better.
See the combat is servicable, but at the start it's rather cumbersome and clunky, you have no range, low damage, you get forced back when you hit something and every enemy deals contact damage. This is all for the Metroidvania style of course, but I can't help but feel making the Nail combat easier from the get go would have helped things. Like it's not bad it's just kind of an annoyance, because you're always feeling "Ugh, when do i upgrade my stuff?" But that's a personal gripe, some others might not be bothered by it.
Music is good very atmospheric. Later in the game you'll find an area that is absolutely eldritch and the sound design sets the eerie factor x100 on top of the story implications. As with the music, the background visuals are top notch, everything is so rustic and post apocalytpic, decaying. There was a lot of effort into making the world as alive(dead?) as possible.
Lots to go on about the game and after 40 hours, I can say it's probably one of my favorite games I've played this year. Easily the best indie game.
Who would I recommend this to? If you like Metroid/Castlevania type games, Dark Souls, Dark Fantasy as a genre, difficult games, platforming, or just a really good story. And it lets you play the way you want to for the most part, it's very flexible in how you approach the world and bosses. I do not recommend this if you don't like these sorts of games though, the game is not easy and will take a lot of deaths and patience to get through. So if you don't have the patience for that, go watch an LP or something.
Almost perfect, my only gripe is the contact damage with all the enemies is really annoying and IMO an outdated concept. But that is a nitpick.
Oh and I just wanted to add, the game is very unique with its setting, style and characters. It's true iconic, not Ubisoft iconic! I have a real love for character designs that are truly unique and memorable.

Alright, so me being a railroader (USA), having years of conductor and engineer exp, I was excited to see that you actually get out of the seat and get on the ground. this was the main selling point for me seeing that 90% of what actually goes on in railroad operations is done from the ground. Switching in yards, riding cars, walking air tests and whatnot, so I finally knuckled down and bought this. Well, theres pros and cons thats for sure.
Cons: The game crashes... a lot. I meet and even surpass the recommended settings to run this game and I can run it on max settings no problem. yet it still crashes. Next comes the on the ground aspect, when switching you have no way of controlling the engine from the ground, as in being like a conductor giving an engineer commands. So you cant climb down and tell your engineer Ahead, or back it up. This means while yes you can get down to line your own switch, youve gotta climb back up to run the controls, tie onto your cars, then climb down and run back there to do your on the ground stuff. Why is there at least not a command feature like forwards and backwards? Next would be the lack of local jobs, its either a yard switcher or road trains. Woooo we get to ride for several hours. Why not have some local jobs where we can go town to town and make set outs or pick ups along the way like in real life? Also why no editor? Thats half the fun is being able to create your own line.
Pros: The game is down right beautiful. From the lighting, to the weather effects, to being able to see every inch of a locomotive cab in full detail. Also from my exp as an engineer, they finally fixed the brake settings in this game unlike in train simulator. Your loco brake actually works now and doesnt take you a quarter mile a 5 mph to stop. You can actually stop in a realistic distance. Being able to actually get out and walk around is a breath of fresh air. Most of a real conductors work is done on the ground, so finally being able to get out of the seat and do things from the ground is awesome. The detail of the locos is amazing, from the cab to the outside of the unit, theyre all done in incredible detail. The track looks great, especially with the rain effects.
Conclusion: This game obviously has its bugs as all games do, but these need worked out. If im running the rig I am, and it crashes theres something wrong. You wont get the hours out of this as you will with train simulator, theres just not that much to do, and the whole having to climb down, do your work on the ground then climb back up, start moving then climb back down is ridiculous. If they eventually add some kind of command function then itd be "shut up and take my money". But until they get the bugs worked out and actually add more to this... save your pennies and just stick with train simulator.

Stronghold Crusader II is quite a good game.
In many ways it is similar to Age of Empires.
It includes a wide range of civilian and military roles.
You have to balance the economic needs of your military versus the morale of your civilian population, the level of which goes up and down, largely depending on how much taxation they are being charged; however, their morale is also impacted by the amount of alcohol and religion you provide them with (not necessarily at the same time).
A high morale level attracts more workers to your settlement, whilst having a low morale level means that workers will leave you and head off for greener pastures.
As with Age of Empires, it is one of those games which you can play for hours and lose track of time.
If you like Age of Empires, then chances are that you'll like this game too.

I thought that this was actually a fantastic game. I will say, however, that I wasn't able to complete it as I originally intended, as an online co-op experience. A friend and I completed a handful of levels, but then the lag between us became excessive. We play other games together fairly regularly, so I felt that this is likely an issue with the game itself. We only finished the game after meeting each other in person. The other issues include a strange mission-selection system that forces you to replay levels you have already beaten to unlock additional content, and a laser turret segment that is next to impossible with standard mouse sensitivity. However, with all that being said, very few games are well-designed from the ground up to be cooperative experiences like this one. On some occasions one player will unlock walkways for the other, one player may have mines and the other a detonator, or one may be able to see certain enemies or obstacles that do not appear on the other's screen. All of these require coordination and communication to execute. However, the soundtrack is totally goofy and may need an overhaul.

Ahhhhhh, Starmade. Where to start?
First off, I have had this game for a long time, I only recently linked it to my steam account, Don't give me any of that"You've only played one and a half hours" Also, Just because a game is in early access/ beta doesn't make it exempt from critisism.
The Good:
-Looks fabulous for a block based game. Shadows, bloom, all of it is great and I love it.
-Intresting in a way that not many othe games can pull off. This means it is stable, works, and has good content.
-Frequent updates. This game gets new content often, and I genuinly beleive the people at schine are working hard.
-Building is fun. In some games, building is a chore. You can be delighted as ideas fly through your head, and possibly your left foot, such "Should I put escape pods?" or "Should I put a turret here?" and so much more.
Now, the bad:
-It gets boring, theres nothing to convince you to build, and after a while, you just get sick of it. What this game needs is a story that gently prods you in the right direction, like  the one in the game Rodina. The proceduraly generated worlds dont have much variety.
-Multiplayer is a cut-throat tedious, and rage inducing experience. You can be a newbie in a server and be killed instantly, or be a pro and griefed to extinction.
-The community is dieing. Servers used to be full of people, hundreds, but today you'll be luckyto find 30.
-It's going to take you  a long time to be able to build the stuff in the screenshots.
In conclusion:
This game is a great concept that hasn't really been driven in the right direction. Some updates and a story would make this game my favorite ever easily. Back to Star Trek Online for now.

A nice little turn based RPG made to (sort of) look like an early 16-bit era JRPG. Combat goes fast and is very well balanced, conveyance is straightforward, difficulty curve is steady, music is okay. Everything works. The level up bonus system gives a nice, tangible way to spec out your team. The combo system adds some good risk management. Battle limits ease the tedium of random encounters while still challenging the player. The writing is good and funny, not actually laughing funny, more of a slight smile funny, but still. On the down side, the level design is abysmal. The dungeons are literally just mazes with no logic to their purpose or nature. The dungeon crawl is also very shallow. Aside from bosses, there are no events, and chests typically just contain boring junk like money or potions or things you could've just bought. But still, it's a nice throwbaack to the classic feel with fresh design sense thrown in. I've payed much more for much worse.

Cons:

For example, he once prevented me from selling a player who's wages were eating into my funds (we'll get onto that in a second). Neither was I permitted to release him. Other times he prevents you from selling young players, constantly has unrealistic expectations for your squad whatever their state, etc.
- Economy sucks - you have "less" - or as I prefer: ZERO control over your income. You cannot upgrade your stadium easily and you don't seem to attract higher attendance even with fantastic results. Player wages eat up the majority of your funds and while the transfer market is closed, and you are warned to "ensure you have a positive balance" to sign new players, you will come to learn that you aren't a manager - you ain't♥♥♥♥♥♥ you're just a plaything for the chairman.
^ If that isn't enough, 95% of the time players on the transfer list won't buy for less than 125-50% of their value, yet the offers you receive for players are normally ~75% of the player's worth.
- Results seem to be very random as I was constantly beating the top sides of my division 2-0, then losing 1-4 to Mansfield Town the following day - same team, same tactics, same fitness. Odd. Sure, there can be randomness, but it just seems too random.
- You cannot choose friendlies and are obliged to do the ones assigned.
- Moral is BS, you cannot improve it in some cases even when playing players every game in correct positions.
- Contracts cannot be changed, and never expire; players cannot be congratulated (and rarely punished) for their performance or conduct. It's because of this that there is no connection between you, the manager, and your "squad". Zilch. None. Nothing. Sad.
- I DON'T WANT TO SHARE WITH FRIENDS, THEY COULDN'T CARE LESS IF I BEAT SWINDON 3-1 AT COUNTRY GROUND (these "encouraging" messages are constant)
- The shop. Bad idea. Just charge a fiver for the game,
What's most frustrating is that with otherwise positive features this could be such a great game.

After playing games of this genre my entire life, I was excited for a throwback to the style of other games that I loved. Unfortunately, Breath of Death VII didn't live up to my expectations.
The one original idea I noticed in the game was the battle mechanic that builds momentum each turn of the battle. Enemies get stronger, and you can build up a combo as long as you don't heal and just keep attacking. While an interesting concept, it ended up removing most semblance of the strategy that exists in turn-based RPGs and turning it into each battle essentially feeling like a race to try and see if you can kill the enemy or boss before having to heal.
That, combined with the short length of the game and the sense of humour that seemed a bit forced, made me fairly disappointed with this title. I would sooner recommend an RPG made with RPG Maker, or that you simply replay the games whose nostalgia this title is trying to capitalize on.

10/10 scary game: Story Time....
There I was, deep in the Cernarus woods, walking for hours with nothing but an M9 pistol with one clip. The moon was shining brightly through the canopy and the winter wind gently rustled the leaves in the trees above. after a while, I thought I was lost, until I saw a blinking red light in the distance through the brush. I started to sprint towards it. As I approached the treeline I noticed hangars and a large opening, an airstrip. I could hear the ocean in the distance, and the waves crashing against the not so soft-sandy beaches. I sit inside a near bush overlooking the airfeild... it had a grass runway... I watched it for a good while before sneaking in. I crawl under a break in the bottom of a wooden wall, and sneak into a tiny shed. I hear footsteps, getting closer, and closer. I load my final mag into my M9 and begin to aim at the door as it swings openthe barrel of an AK-74 is sticking out from behind the door as it slowly creeps in. I see a hand and I open fire. I chase the retreating arm outside and finish the guy off... I pick up his gun and start to run away as fast as possible, heart pounding... I can hear the sound of bullets flying past me and can see their impacts just infront of me. I make it back into the woods, lucky to be alive... as I finally calm my breathing, I start to hear something in the distance... I look to my left and I see that s search light is approaching me quickly, I start to run away when I run into a patrol in the woods, who turn and open fire on me, I now have the whole russian army after me at this point.... the helicopter is firing everything it has at me, and infantry, cars, tanks... anything you can name was chasing me to my final breath... after this... after finally dying due to helicopter rockets... I believe many years have been taken off of my life... and I can already see grey growing in my hair...
10/10 would face the russian army again.

I would consider myself a pretty big Final Fantasy fan at this point. Type-O was a game I really didn't know what to expect of, and I can gladly say I was pleasantly surprised (for the most part).
I'll get the negatives out of the way first. The game is vague, convoluted and very confusing almost all the way through. You don't really connect with any characters throughout the entire game, there's not enough back story and substance to any of the characters I found. The camera will make you violently sick if you don't adjust your camera distance and turn OFF motion blur. Some battles are just infuriating and incredibly cheap. You will be forced to load your game at some points just to readjust your party abilities just so you can actually damage an enemy. Throughout 30 hours of game time I have not yet found one single phoenix down, why.
All in all the game is very enjoyable and has a nice combat system. However, the game will not tell you anything about progression and items so you're really left to learn it yourself. I didn't know you could upgrade and gain new abilities until well over half way into the game (15-20 odd hours). If you can get it cheap, then definitely buy.

Hollow Knight had been described to me as 2D Dark Souls with a unique artstyle. In the end I don't quite agree with the description. I'd describe it more as a platformer and exploring game with combat elements. Combat is very common, close to every room has some form of enemy but the combat system itself is not very complex, it largely consists of timing your basic swordswing and then dodging away or jumping over your target, there's some additional skills you find / learn throughout the game but I hardly used them. Having been described as similar to Dark Souls I expected the game to be difficult and that I'd die a lot, that was not the case. It was somewhere between easy and medium difficulty I'd say. I barely died which I guess is a good thing as retrieving your Geo - the game's equivalent of souls - could be quite a chore. So far I've been fairly critical so I'll mention the game's virtues - which there are quite a few of. The world is unique and interesting, a large part of this could be attributed to the game's beautiful artstyle which is simplistic but visually interesting and varied. The story is ambigious and quite subtle allowing for extensive speculation throughout and even after the game. Character progression is handled well in my opinion, you don't level up - instead you find new artifacts or upgrade your weapon through a smith to get more powerful. The games biggest strength in my opinion however is it's simplicity, I already briefly mentioned this talking about the combat and artstyle but there's more to it. Basically what we start the game with is the ability to swing our sword, heal and jump and with just those three mechanics the game just works. A lot of games are overdesigned and have overwhelming systems and combat but Hollow Knight keeps it basic and I find it admirable. Hopefully this review can be somewhat helpful, it's my first game writing this extensively. To finish, even though I may have gone on about the what I thought some of the consequences were I want you to know that the positives far outweigh the negatives and that this is a truly great game.

is a first person one versus all multiplayer experience that takes a radical departure from from the shooter genre.  Boasting a controversial gimmick where the game servers will shut down indefinitely when the total number of lives run out (as of now, around 215 million), the concept behind
is unique, to say the least.  However, given how difficult it even is to find a match online due to the woefully empty player base, there's no chance of the game ending any time in the near future.
All of that aside,
manages only to excel in mediocrity.  There is all but one game mode, a one vs all where players  vie to find the light artifact and fend off the other players, the shadow monsters .  Only three maps are available at the moment, so
does feel a bit light on content. Barring the short tutorial, the game is multiplayer only, yet even finding an active game has been an exercise in futility given the almost non-existent player base.
If you actually do manage to find a game, upon entering the match, the players are thrust into the role of shadow creatures, racing each other to the light artifact to become the light carrier.   The light carrier can kill the shadows with their movement based kinetic powered light gun (a flashlight), though shadows are immune when they aren't moving.   The person who survives as the light bearer the longest wins the game, so it’s a relatively simple game in execution.
The controls, though relatively easy to master are clunky at best, and the game as a whole feels slow in execution.  Maps feel too large to find players, and the movement as a shadow monster feels a bit disorienting with the amount of head bobbing (though this can be turned off in the options).  The graphics and sound don't fare much better either, and while serviceable, are not exactly anything to write home about.  When it works, the game's presentation is acceptable, yet bland overall.
There are a myriad of technical problems in the game as well, some crippling, and some just annoying.  I experienced several crashes to the desktop and black screens when attempting to start the game or join a match.  In its current state, it seems to be a gamble whether the game will work or not, though some issues encountered could unlikely be due to Windows 10.
Either way, it would be difficult to recommend
in its current state.  There's not much content in the game, and given its relatively high price on the Steam Store ($16.99/€16.99), this game should be skipped unless you're the type of person that enjoys frustration.  Though the concept remains an interesting one, the lack of an online community ultimately kills this bland multiplayer-only title.
Overall, a
.  Not Recommended.

Most people that've played the original Shadowgrounds can agree that it's a hidden gem among isometric shooters. The game has pretty much everything going for it; engaging gameplay, immersive atmosphere, a great soundtrack, and a ton of blood. For an older game from 2006, it's aged remarkably well despite not being able to play it in a 1080p or higher resolution. It's only right that one should assume the same success from its follow up release, Shadowgrounds Survivor, which was released a year later.
Taking place once again on Jupiter's moon, Ganymede, the player will control three characters over the course of 9 chapters that are split into 24 levels. They're among the last remaining humans on the celestial body, who have to fight through the alien forces that are threatening to overrun it. By order of appearance, gamers will control soldier Luke "Marine" Giffords, pest control agent Bruno "Napalm" Lastmann, and scout Isabel "Sniper" Larose. Regarded as a spin-off sequel, Shadowgrounds Survivor doesn't have much barring on the original storyline, and to be quite honest it doesn't have much of a story at all despite its many cutscenes and voice acted segments.
We're going to do this review in the style of the good, the bad, and the ugly, in that order. The good here is that Frozenbyte returned with all of the signature gameplay from the series' sophomore release, and they also introduced some new elements as well. New to this expansion is the ability to level up each survivor individually, and the ability to unlock character specific upgrades. This in tandem with the older function to upgrade weapons makes for a slightly more RPG styled experience, and it works fairly well despite the limited amount of unlocks available. The game also has an incredible, thick atmosphere that has been enhanced thanks to upgraded environment elements such as heavy rain, lightning, and snowstorms. Likewise, the music and ambient layers of the title are superior in comparison to the former release. Lastly, each of the 24 levels takes you on a new journey in a new location, which is quite impressive given the age of the game. These three latter ingredients are probably the best things that Shadowgrounds Survivor has going for it. I should also mention that this title can be played in 1080p resolution, so that's a plus.
Sadly, this title does have more of the bad than the good. Long gone are the big maps that were worth exploring in Shadowgrounds, they've been replaced by very linear and short landscapes. Each level will last anywhere from 5-10 minutes at most, perhaps a little longer if it's a wave based level. This leads me to the next point, Shadowgrounds Survivor now has a wave based mechanic, and you will find yourself more often than not fighting off wave after wave of aliens. This takes away the horror factor that was instilled in the original game, as it's never a guessing game as to whether or not you're going to be up against an enemy. A big reward that came from exploring in the first Shadowgrounds was finding PDA logs that gave a deeper aspect to the story, well those have been taken out of this follow up. They're instead replaced by cutscenes that don't tell much of a story, and some brief dialogue; it's all very shallow in comparison. There's also not as many weapons, and each character has three that they carry; pistols, a minigun, flamethrower, plasma rifle, railgun, assault rifle, and rocket launcher.
Now, lastly, we come to the ugly. This game does have a crashing problem, and it also has visual issues. During a mission with Bruno where I was in the sewers, I was seeing double... literally. Two of Bruno, two of each monster, two of every pick up. In all fairness, it was the only level that I encountered this issue, but it still made for quite a disorienting experience. There's also no longer a manual save mechanic, it has been instead replaced by game created save points that are only at the start of each level; if you die, you go back to the beginning, and that really blows. Despite having a leveling system, you can actually reach an experience point cap per level far before you reach the end of it, which defeats the purpose entirely. Rather than lasting for upwards of ten hours, this title can be completed in as little as 2-3, with very little replay factor; you can find "secrets" to unlock for a bonus mode, but they're all arbitrary things like playing the game in black and white or unlimited ammo on your next playthrough. There's also a survivor mode but it's just more wave based stuff that this series was not built on.
The original Shadowgrounds really had it all; a horrific and gripping sci-fi atmosphere, tons of blood, a decent enough storyline with logs that filled in the gaps, tons of weapons, huge explorable maps, manual saves, and even bosses with mechanics. Shadowgrounds Survivor has built upon the atmosphere of the original, somehow manages to be less gore-filled, the story is very shallow with no log pick-ups, hardly any exploration rewards, minimal weapons, small maps, auto-saves at the beginning of each level, and the bosses have been replaced by waves that are frankly boring. The RPG-like elements aren't even that well developed, and it's hard to believe there's an EXP cap on every level. To be very blunt, Shadowgrounds Survivor should only be played if you're really reaching the bottom of the isometric shooter barrel.

The game is worth the buy and the playthrough if only to see how far the series has come and how completely off base its become. The mechanics and inclusion of somewhat intelligent AI blows its main competitor at the time (Medal of Honor) out of the water. The environments/maps are also quite massive, but are not as diverse as the MoH titles were. Though the missions were straight forward, the story is pretty weak. Clearly, IW recognized this as the big issue when trying to combine the game aspects of how to fight and what you’re fighting for, and this became perfected later on in the series in later iterations.
For some reason, what really stuck out to me about this game (even after playing countless modern FPSs) is how smooth the vehicle combat was.  It was fair for the most part, but you’d get hit randomly and it would raise the stakes enough for you to make your shots count and rely on the game’s minimalist in-car cover system.
It felt better than 9 out of the 10 scripted car chases in games these days. I guess they just don’t make them like they used to.
I should also note that you can play these games on your monitor’s native resolution. You just have to mess around with the .cfg file under the display height and width settings.

Before the real review I think I have to highlight a couple of things:
This game was born for PSP. This affect many aspects of the game some obvious like graphic and characters movement during dialogs (or no movement, they just stand still); some less obvious, for example I am pretty sure that many aspects of the game would have been different if thought for a console, like the time progression in academia or the side characters mini storilines.
If you read the review you can see the 90% - 95% of the "Not Recommended" ones are about:
1) the Camer Control (problem solved in a game update),
2) bad porting because graphic was not improved enough for their tastes
3) bad porting because of performance issues (I am pretty sure that at least someone of these was doing something wrong like using the intel integrated video card). I had no performance issue using a mid level laptop 3-4 years old.
4) 30 fps. Again, it was created for PSP and they could not change this.
And one last note: this game was born with a controller in mind. You can use the mouse+keyboard, but if you have one use a controller (or buy the steam controller, i like it).
REVIEW:
GRAPHIC: watch the trailers and the sreenshots: that's the graphic level. Personally for me is fine. But I don't care about the graphic, I didn't buy this game for that.
GAMPLAY:
here we have to distinguish between combat, RTS and the events/exploring the world.
Combat: I think it is very cool, each character (14) has an unique style of combat and this make changing the primary char really fun and often needed. Then the fact that you can't ressurrect them if they die during missions is nice, since each death makes you closer to defeat (winning with the last standing char is amazing). There is also a killsight system that let you do a lot more damage if you hit the enemy at the right moment (for example while he is performing a particular action). My opinion is: I love the combat style of FFType0. Fun fast but also tactical and never monotonous.
RTS missions: In this game there are RST mission (DOTA style), I found them cool and nice to do something a bit different every now and then. Also those make you feel the "war" that is rampaging in Orience and is not only on the background since you will participate in the battles to conquer cities and regions.
Events: finally there are the events you can discover around academia and orience between missions. You have a time limit and each event you activate (dialogs, scenes, exiting academia) will cost some time. Do not worry you will have plenty of time to do almost all the events. And the game is born to be played many times: for example doing an event you already saw in a previous playtrought will cost no time. And there many things that could not be done during the first playtrought like the expert trial mission or the code crimson missions. Personally I am not a fun of this "time cost" system but I don't hate it either; it is
STORY:
everyone has his opinion about what a "Real Final Fantasy" is. For me is the story. If the story is bad or worse if it doesn't exhist (and I am watching you FF XII and XIII) that is not a real FF for me. Well this game (my personal opinion) is the first FF game since FF X.
One of the things that I liked most is the fact that in this world when people dies they are forgotten. This makes it easier for everyone to fight but it also scares them in many ways and some of the most interesting stories told in FF type 0 starts from this loss. But this is not the only things that makes the story of FF strong and powerful. The world of orience is a world at war and they describe this state really well, making you feel it (I think you can begin to understand now why FF type 0 is considered the "darkest" FF).
14 characters may seems a lot, and for sure I can say the some of them are not shown enough; but still they hardly feel bidimensional. And while some may receive little time, Machina, Rem and Ace are shown in all their depth.
IN SHORT:
I really liked Final Fantasy Type-0. Yes it suffers a lot from being a PSP game, but still the gameplay is probably one of the best ones in the saga (if you like action) and the story, while it may not be told as well as it was in FF X, is deep, is strong and is there.
Overall a really good playthrough. The writing, gameplay, humor, everything really, is great.

Shadow Warrior is one of the best FPS games that I've ever played in my life! You take control over Lo Wang, a cocky guy who has to do some exchange for his boss. Things are going sour, you're getting ambushed and you end up teaming up with equally cocky demon (sic!). That's the beginning of really interesting story that I'm not going to spoil here.
Let's just say that your first (and main) weapon is a katana. And boy, did they make this weapon enjoyable to use :) You also have guns. Lots of guns. Machine gun, flamethrower, crossbow, ninja stars, freaking disembodied demon's head... And you can hold all of them, which is rare for games released nowadays.
You also have 3 types of upgrades (and 3 'currencies' so to speak to use for said upgrades). Weapon enchancements, powers and skills. You can unlock special attacks, healing boost, defensive moves, special powerful katana attacks, variety is stunning.
The game encourages exploration. There are a lot of secrets scattered through the game there's also few easter eggs (for example: try to disturb two bunnies which have intimate moment together ;)
Controls are nice and responsive. Your special moves are done by pressing certain combination of buttons. It's fluent and simple. You also have dash move, which comes in handy suprisingly often.
Graphics and aesthetic are great.
Enemies are crazy and satisfying to kill. There are also 3 big boss battles, and I mean big. Like you are fighting an enemy who's like 50 meters high :P
I have only two pet peeves with this game:
First - at a certain point you can clearly see the 'ambush' sort of gameplay that they tried to use. Like you find some important object and bam, it's an ambush, enemies swarming you left and right. It's not Call of Duty bad, where if you don't move the enemies will respawn infinetely (well, disregard :P they will until you kill the spawner :P). Nah, it's obvious what they tried to do. It's not horrible, but pretty transparent and somewhat annoying at times. Good that killing enemies is so fun :P
Second - there's no map. The game is quite linear, but there are still some parts of the game where I just got lost and didn't know what to do next (usually it had something to do with finding a certain spot to plant explosives or press a button on the wall somwhere)
All in all - Shadow Warrior is really great game and it saddens me that crap like Call of Duty sells millions of copies and enjoyable gems like Shadow Warrior are neglected.

The flock is a rather fun game that's reminiscent of Dr. Who's Weeping Angels. Add a bit of Aliens, a dash of apocalyptic mystery, and you've got an interesting game. Yes, there is a finite population, and a theoretical "ending" to the game. However, millions of players would need to die in order for that to happen, which doesn't look likely in the near future.
THAT said, it's a rather fun game. The game is definitely something to play alone in the dark. The first time I turned around and saw a statue (or was it?) staring at me, I nearly lost my s***. The tone that it makes when you see one of the Flock standing there just watching you is creepy enough.
As one of the Flock, your goal is to become the light bearer by eating him. As the Carrier, your goal is to stay alive long enough to cleanse the area of darkness. Shine the light on one of the Flock, and they have to turn to stone. If they don't, they die. As one of the Flock, you've got the ability to call out to other Flock, or you can clone yourself and create a statue in your place, and then teleport back to the clone, leaving a statue where you just were. It's extremely fun to mindf**k other players using those tactics.
In general, super creepy, and super fun.
8/10

SHORT VERSION:
This game is absolutely brilliant if you love building and just building. However, it quickly loses its charm when you realize that you can't actually really DO anything with the ship(s) you put all of your hard work into. Come back in a while and see if it's any better, if you like. The game still is in alpha stage development.
VERY LONG VERSION:
This game is not recommendable unless you love building for the sake of building.
Expanding on that idea of loving to build, Starmade has one of the best set of tools for building whatever the fudge you want in this game. The not horribly demanding placement of blocks in order for a ship to work allows for a fair bit of flexibility in making a ship that works alright. The most complex blocks to use (reactor stabalizers) only need to be placed a certain distance from another block type (reactor blocks). The inclusion of the advanced build mode features accessible by holding down lcontrol also significantly enhance your abilities to create by allowing you to define symmetry planes, place hundreds of blocks at once, copy n' paste and more! Various systems such as rails and logic also give you the ability to create a lot of different functioning mechanisms as simple as an elevator or password-protected door or as complicated as Space Monopoly (yes, someone did do that). It's even possible to create a basic computer on your ships to execute commands from a console in order to lock down, flash red alerts, undock drones, and whatever else you would want to do!
The main issue with the game is the lack of survival gameplay; there's not much to do with those ships you made.
There's no real reason to explore after seeing all the different ships and stations because everything that is randomly generated is pretty much the same old stuff. There's nothing like nebulae or ion storms that could provide navigational challenge or special gaseous resources, crashed ships with flight data or blueprints, or dangerous pirate territory stacked with loot (pirates now don't count because the danger level of pirates is pretty much constant wherever anyone goes, and there's no real reason to raid them). Nothing is there to push players to create ships to take on new challenges.
Nothing ever really happens in the galaxy, either. Every system in the universe of StarMade is pretty much the same and contains all the resources you ever will need, so there's no reason to invade anyone else or negotiate/trade with anyone else for resources. Everything just grinds to a standstill in the galaxy, and nothing interesting ever really happens in a standard game that will require resources to deal with and, therefore, ships.
Please do note that the game is completely free in its early access stages. Just click the "download demo" button to get the full version. You may as well try it out to judge it for yourself, and if you don't like it stop by after a while and see if something was added that catches your eye.

Having spent some time around the various racing sims, I can say this is not the most realistic, not the best looking and not the best feeling (Force Feedback) sim out there. But currently it's my favourite,
The game is free, but you have to pay for content like cars and tracks. Considering that you probably will have a few favorite rides and some favourite places to race, you don't need to buy everyting, and with that in mind the pricing is reasonable (just buy a points package and get the content you are interested in). To get everything you have to spend a significant amount of cash, but it's still cheaper than playing iRacing or something like Project CARS / Assetto Corsa with all DLC considering the amoutn of content that is available.
Now for the game itself. The graphics are good, though not mind blowing, but considering that you will be focused on turning that wheel and operating the pedals, you will forget about visuals fast. The sound on the other hand is the best in the market hands down.
Handling is fairly realistic, though not hardcore difficult like rFactor 2, with good Force Feedback once configured properly. Though it is possible to enhoy the game with a controller, a wheel is highly recommended.
Now for the sweet parts - contrary to other sims, there is a good combination of cars and tracks. You will not see stuff like 1 car per class or useless roadcars that go slow and spin out all the time - no Ferraris and SLS AMGs, no drifting. This is all about racing. And racing is good. The AI is one of the better ones, so you will not get divebombed by crazy maniacs all the time, and the difficulty setting will accomodate players of all skill levels. Not the best AI in the market, but quite good and most of all fun,
The bad stuff? No night racing or rain. Not really a big deal, since in other sims these types of races a cool to look at, but mostly hard and frustrating. Perhaps the biggest issue to me is the lack of a dynamic racing line, where the track rubbers up in places where cars drive and you have more grip there. Not really a problem, but once you try something like this in rFactor 2, you do notice it other games. Raceroom also lacks open-wheelers and does not have many classic cars, but that is to change soon. Another thing is a full flag rules system is still to be addes at some point.
All in all, of all the new generation of racing sims, Raceroon seems most fun thanks to a good selection of cars and tracks and good AI. If you are looking to get into simracing this is defo the game to try. Other sims might have better graphics or laser scanned tracks, but not the AI Racerrom has nor the amount of actual racing content we see here.

Amazing. one of the few games in recent years to pull me in.
If you enjoy games with tons of content, that are actually challenging, and are completely polished, look no further.
Hollow knight manages to tell one of the most compelling stories that I've witnessed in a game, with no narration or hour long cut scenes. It's probably the minimalism that makes it so unique, the moments that stick with you are stuble and are a fleeting moment. Looking out a window into a dead city, watching a friend turn into one of the monsters you've become so numb to slaughtering in the hundreds, corpses hudled together in a corner of the map.
For me these felt more real than any story based game I've experienced.
Which is funny because this isnt really a story based game, it has some of the smoothest combat I've seen. Just when you've started to grasp how to fight enemies with minimal damage in an area, you're thrown a curveball: a new area with completely different enemies, coming back to an area only to find all the bugs have changed their appearance and fighting style.  When you do something badass, you feel badass. Probably because the controls are so tight every movement feels like your own. Every counter feels like your design, because it is! There isnt a set way to beat any boss or counter a certain move, you make your own way: meticulously sidestep your opponent until an oppourtunity arises, or go in full rambo swinging your nail left and right hitting anything that moves.
Yet it probably isn't the combat or the story that makes this game top notch in my opinion, its the feeling of discovery. Every corner could bring a new fight, or a secret passage. Every new area only connects to other new ones waiting to be explored. Every small victory is rewarded, every act of curiostity is well spent. I have spent hours just aimlessly exploring the huge game world, finding as many nooks and small peices of lore as I could. Only to think "I wonder if there is something over there" when looking at my map, and finding a whole new game area. This is why this game is so special to me, why I hope to 100% it, and continue to when the amazing devs release more content.
(if anyone is wondering why I have so little hours, I spent 35 hours on a pirated copy before finally saying to myself that this game is a masterpiece and I needed to own it for real)

There really is no debate. Football Manager is better than Soccer Manager. It has more depth, options, and has been around a lot longer. It also costs more. A lot more. Especially for those “faithful” fans that buy every year’s new iteration that only contains minor updates. This just baffles me, whether it’s FM, Madden, or NBA 2K. $60 every year for the same game? Rarely do such sport franchises make any earth shattering changes that in my opinion justify buying it every single year. Roster changes don’t count as earth shattering in my book. I own Football Manager 2014 and have played 562 hours on it and I could happily play it for several more years before needing to purchase the latest iteration. Especially since it comes with a data editor that many people are willing to make those updated roster changes for you. So, how do you dethrone this ruthless tyrant that has a stranglehold on the soccer (ahem, football for most of the world) simulation management industry?
Make it free-to-play (F2P), simple to play, and as an added bonus, make it similar to the very first versions of the ruthless king, like back when he was a charming prince. Soccer Manager has a very Championship Manager (Football Manager was initially called Championship Manager before a split between the developers and publisher) feel to it. My first introduction to sports sims was Championship Manager 2 back in 1995 so there’s definitely a bit of nostalgia that helps boost Soccer Manager in a positive manner. It also is F2P and has updated rosters. Since I “only” have FM2014 I was able to try out my Tottenham club with their latest real world roster without having to shell out another $50. While you do have to pay for certain things like scouting faster and additional load/save slots, none of them will stop you from playing and enjoying the game. One of the great pros of Soccer Manager is that there are very few media interviews!! Football Manager, in attempting to make you feel like you really are the manager on the sidelines, has created a very “un-fun” process of 20 questions (the answers to which impact how your players will perform so you better answer them correctly!!) before each match and several after the match, and some more questions for you to answer when you’re not in a match, just because, that’s what managers have to deal with! Well, I just want to buy players and play matches! Soccer Manager gets you back to the basics. Yes, Football Manager does have a Classic mode, which is what I exclusively use now, but it just feels like Football Manager has gotten away from what their game used to be about.
Football Manager just hasn’t had much competition lately and maybe that is the reason why each version since 2012 seems to be getting worse and worse based on reviews and complaints that I’ve read. So if anything Soccer Manager will push Football Manager to be better. At the end of the day, Football Manager is better than Soccer Manager. But, Soccer Manager is free and with updated rosters, so give it a shot!!

Dungeon Defenders is a game that I developed a love-hate relationship with. On one hand, it's a class-based multiplayer action RPG with tower defense elements and is a lot of fun to play with friends of similar levels. However the game has many elements which tend to be detrimental to the experience. For one thing, the game is very grind-heavy. Whether you're getting new gear, or gaining a new level, or trying to get a really obscure achievement for a rare pet, the grind will make you feel like you're playing a Chinese MMO. Second, the sheer amount of player levels means unless all players are the same level, someone will feel like one is carrying the other. Third, much of the content of the game is locked behind so much DLC that it would give Train Simulator a run for its money. Fourth, the game is not very fun playing solo and you cannot even get achievements solo unless you play online.
Dungeon Defenders is a really huge timesink, and I know plenty of gamers who enjoy that, but at the end of day I never felt a sense of real accomplishment despite the sheer amount of "progression" I made in my characters. At higher levels I grew bored with the sheer monotony of the game, watching my towers decimate entire rows of bad guys who only know how to march like lemmings over and over again. In the end, I found the action-oriented nature of Orcs Must Die and Orcs Must Die 2 to be far more fulfilling for my tastes.

Did somebody say "hardcore strategy"? If they did, they were probably referring to this game. I haven't played the table-top original, but I can say that you need to really think when you play this Steam version of Space Hulk. I mean, REALLY think a few moves ahead as though you were playing Chess, because this has an unforgiving and challenging dice-roll system for combat that does not favour the player as in other Warhammer/Citadel franchise games (i.e. Dawn of War II). In terms of gameplay, it's a top-down turn-based layout that somewhat resembles a table-top game. Your units have a limited number of moves per turn including combat abilities. The menus and in-game controls are fairly intuitive, and there's an in-picture Terminator shoulder-cam that gives you a first person perspective of the map which is very cool (It's a bit like watching "Aliens" when the marines are exploring the abandoned complex). So, if you've an abundance of patience and want to test your strategic skill, play this game. ***

Shadow Warrior is one of the best FPS games that I've ever played in my life! You take control over Lo Wang, a cocky guy who has to do some exchange for his boss. Things are going sour, you're getting ambushed and you end up teaming up with equally cocky demon (sic!). That's the beginning of really interesting story that I'm not going to spoil here.
Let's just say that your first (and main) weapon is a katana. And boy, did they make this weapon enjoyable to use :) You also have guns. Lots of guns. Machine gun, flamethrower, crossbow, ninja stars, freaking disembodied demon's head... And you can hold all of them, which is rare for games released nowadays.
You also have 3 types of upgrades (and 3 'currencies' so to speak to use for said upgrades). Weapon enchancements, powers and skills. You can unlock special attacks, healing boost, defensive moves, special powerful katana attacks, variety is stunning.
The game encourages exploration. There are a lot of secrets scattered through the game there's also few easter eggs (for example: try to disturb two bunnies which have intimate moment together ;)
Controls are nice and responsive. Your special moves are done by pressing certain combination of buttons. It's fluent and simple. You also have dash move, which comes in handy suprisingly often.
Graphics and aesthetic are great.
Enemies are crazy and satisfying to kill. There are also 3 big boss battles, and I mean big. Like you are fighting an enemy who's like 50 meters high :P
I have only two pet peeves with this game:
First - at a certain point you can clearly see the 'ambush' sort of gameplay that they tried to use. Like you find some important object and bam, it's an ambush, enemies swarming you left and right. It's not Call of Duty bad, where if you don't move the enemies will respawn infinetely (well, disregard :P they will until you kill the spawner :P). Nah, it's obvious what they tried to do. It's not horrible, but pretty transparent and somewhat annoying at times. Good that killing enemies is so fun :P
Second - there's no map. The game is quite linear, but there are still some parts of the game where I just got lost and didn't know what to do next (usually it had something to do with finding a certain spot to plant explosives or press a button on the wall somwhere)
All in all - Shadow Warrior is really great game and it saddens me that crap like Call of Duty sells millions of copies and enjoyable gems like Shadow Warrior are neglected.
